content:
tim_support: heads up — multiple EU1 customers reporting increased 502/504s and auth failures since ~08:10 UTC. Intermittent timeouts, high retry counts. Customer screenshots attached in support tickets. :rotating_light:
kevin_oncall: oncall here, thanks. any common request_ids or gateway node?
maria_sre: I grabbed recent gateway logs for eu1-edge. Pattern: TLS handshake timeouts and TCP retransmits. Example log:
```
2026-03-15T08:12:04Z eu1-edge-03 gateway[pid=4721]: req=xyz123 id=01F... status=502 err="tls handshake failed: read tcp 10.0.3.45:443->192.0.2.18:52344: i/o timeout"
2026-03-15T08:12:05Z eu1-edge-03 kernel: tcp: retransmit timeout, 12 retransmits
```
jonathan_prod: customers also saw spikes in auth failures (401/403) — could be due to replayed requests or truncated TLS causing token parsing errors.
networking: we see a spike in BGP update churn reported by provider NetTransitX in EU1-azb at ~08:09–08:18 UTC. AS path changes + flaps to a subset of egress peers. Initial telemetry: increased packet loss (0.5–3% peak), transient reordering. Provider ticket opened, they report partial microbursts on egress.
deploy-bot: reroute-trigger initiated by kevin_oncall at 08:22 UTC — redirecting new traffic from eu1-edge-03 -> eu1-edge-07 for 10m canary.
kevin_oncall: mitigation done. can we get repro steps so support can reproduce and confirm?
tim_support: repro steps I used against hosted inference (redwood-api):
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"test latency","max_tokens":16}' &
done; wait
```
Repeat a few times from an EU1 region VM — observe 5–10% 502s, lots of `SSL: certificate verify failed` or `empty reply from server` in curl verbose output.
alice_research: I ran an mtr from a repro host to eu1-edge-03 and saw packet loss increasing at provider hop: 
```
HOST: repro-eu1                                         Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1. 10.0.0.1                                               0.0%    20    0.4   0.6   0.3   1.5   0.3
 2. 198.51.100.5                                           0.0%    20    1.2   1.8   0.8   9.8   2.3
 3. 203.0.113.22                                         2.5%    20   10.8  12.4   9.9  45.1   8.9  <-- provider hop
 4. eu1-edge-03                                          0.0%    20    3.2   3.9   3.0   8.2   1.2
```
maria_sre: tcpdump snippet on eu1-edge-03 (filtered):
```
10:12:04.123456 IP 192.0.2.18.52344 > 10.0.3.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
10:12:04.223789 IP 192.0.2.18.52344 > 10.0.3.45.443: Flags [F.], ack 1, win 65535, length 0  <-- early FINs / resets
```
networking: NetTransitX confirmed they had a partial asymmetry causing retransmits and occasional blackholing on a small subset of prefixes (we're in the affected pool). They pushed a filter/adj-change at 08:24 UTC that reduced update churn.
kevin_oncall: mitigation checklist done: canary reroute, increased gateway keepalive from 20s -> 60s, HAProxy timeout tweaks, and enabled fallback to dedicated-path if TLS handshake fails 3x. Monitoring: error rate dropped ~60% after 08:26 UTC.
onboarding-bot: incident annotation: provider=BGP_NX, impact=hosted_inference_eu1, status=mitigated, tickets=[NTX-4567].
eva_sales: got a few angry escalations from enterprise customers mentioning billing windows failing and retries causing duplicate invoices — can we confirm if requests retried by clients resulted in duplicate billing events?
jonathan_prod: billing system keys requests by idempotency-key header for generation calls; however some customers don't send one. We should identify request_ids that had multiple successful downstream model execs. maria_sre: I pulled a sample of request_ids showing 2 model-exec entries for same client timestamp window; looks like client retried after early 502 and backend accepted later — that caused double billing.
tim_support: action items for support: 1) ask customers to use Idempotency-Key; 2) provide repro curl above and recommend backoff 2s -> exponential; 3) share incident timeline + RC.
maria_sre: permanent followups: (a) work with networking to enforce egress path diversity for eu1-edge fleet, (b) add heuristics in gateway to avoid accepting duplicate model execs when same request_id arrives within 5s and previous exec pending, (c) add more detailed TLS-level metrics per edge node.
alice_research: adding note — some models with long handshake preloads (larger KV cache warmups) were more sensitive to mid-handshake resets, consider keeping lighter preloads for gateway-proxied traffic.
kevin_oncall: closing notes: provider issued RCA pointing to transient hardware queue saturation on one of their transit routers causing reorder/packet drops. We ramped fallbacks, changed timeouts, and request duplication reduced. Assign follow-ups: networking (long-term path diversity), runtime (duplicate exec heuristic), support (customer comms).
eva_sales: pls share a short customer-facing summary I can send to impacted accounts.
tim_support: will draft and post in #incidents-postmortems.
kevin_oncall: thanks all. monitoring will keep this open 24h. :thumbsup:
